images.title: Direct path or roundabout
images.purpose: Show that going straight from tent to tree is shorter than going via the pole.
images.composition: Three simple objects in a triangle layout on white, with two paths drawn clearly.
exact_structure: A flat tent icon on the left in amber (#E69F00), a flat tree icon on the right in green (#009E73), and a flat pole icon at the top centre in grey (#6B7280).
A short straight reddish purple (#CC79A7) line (the direct path) from the tent to the tree along the bottom, with an arrowhead at the tree.
A longer two segment teal (#0072B2) path from the tent up to the pole and then down to the tree, with arrowheads.
The direct path is visibly shorter than the two segment path.
No distances or numbers are drawn.
rejection: the roundabout path drawn shorter than or equal to the direct one
more than one pole, tent or tree
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The direct straight path is the shortest way between two points.
images.description: A tent, a tree and a pole with a short direct path and a longer path via the pole.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which path a walker would take, then see that two sides together are longer than the third.

image_decisions.why: A story scene makes the triangle inequality idea intuitive before any numbers.
